question: An engineer must perform a nondisruptive software upgrade on a dual supervisor Cisco Nexus 7000 Series Switch. What is the cause of the upgrade being disruptive?
options: Attempt to simultaneously upgrade more than thee cards
Change to the configuration settings or the network connections during the upgrade process
The show install all impact command is not issued before the upgrade
The kickstart image is installed by using the install all kickstart image system image command
theory: An ISSU is only guaranteed nondisruptive when the configuration and topology stay stable throughout the process — NX-OS locks the configuration on a vPC peer specifically because a mid-upgrade configuration or connectivity change can invalidate the state synchronization between the old and new control plane, forcing the switch to fall back to a disruptive reload or protocol renegotiation. Exceeding a card-count limit, skipping the impact check, or which install command is used are operational mistakes, but it is specifically changing configuration or network connections mid-upgrade that turns an otherwise-eligible ISSU disruptive. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Nondisruptive ISSU Requirements)
